items.summary: ToMAS is a pilot failure-grounded Theory-of-Mind evaluation package derived from MAST FC2 inter-agent misalignment failures in multi-agent LLM systems.   This deposit includes: 39 CLEAN training items 28 held-out Magentic/GAIA items 39 Coord-RL (LLM-Coordination ToM) training items four-criterion convertibility annotation rubric 18-item reliability pilot coding sheet (Cohen's κ = 0.92) ROUGE-L binary scoring scripts GRPO training script (train_condition.py) training reward logs and adapter/train-compare diagnostics v1.1 added conversion rationales for all 28 held-out items. v1.2 adds train_condition.py, GRPO reward logs, the Coord-RL training file, and adapter/train-compare diagnostics requested for the accompanying paper. Items are derived/converted/modified from MAST-Data (Hugging Face: mcemri/MAST-Data; cemri2025mast) under CC-BY-4.0. Users must attribute both ToMAS (this deposit) and MAST-Data. Coord-RL items additionally adapt ToM questions from LLM-Coordination (Agashe et al., NAACL Findings 2025). This package does not include model checkpoints or the full MAST dump. It supports the pilot benchmark-construction and training-feasibility study described in the accompanying paper.

items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: Essay Five of the Spine, and its last. Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.

items.summary: The paper addresses an ambiguity in chaos diagnostics. A positive Lyapunov exponent establishes local instability and the failure of exact point prediction, but it does not show whether chaotic motion can carry a system across the boundary that defines operational failure. The authors distinguish thin chaos, where local instability remains confined, from thick chaos, where chaotic transport becomes failure-relevant, with transitional chaos as the warning regime between them. To make this distinction operational, they introduce the thinness index, which compares the amount of chaotic transport in a coherence-relevant variable over a chosen timescale with the displacement required to reach failure. The paper develops a step-by-step protocol: define an operational timescale, measure local instability, identify a coherent region, choose a transport variable, estimate chaotic transport, define a failure scale, compute the index, assess uncertainty, and interpret the result. Three applications illustrate the approach. A MEMS resonator shows how chaotic amplitude fluctuations can remain well below the pull-in margin. A celestial Trojan system shows how chaotic libration need not imply escape over a given horizon. A mode-locked laser shows how phase jitter can remain within locking tolerance despite local chaos. In each case, the index distinguishes harmless local irregularity from transport that threatens function. The paper stresses several benefits. The index is quantitative, interpretable as the fraction of the failure margin consumed by chaos, timescale-relative, function-relative, comparative across domains, and useful for early warning and control. It does not replace Lyapunov exponents or transport theory but complements them. The limitations are explicit: the index depends on the chosen coherent region, failure boundary, transport variable, and timescale. It measures scale but not topology, and uncertainty matters near the transition. The conclusion is that chaos becomes dangerous not when it appears but when it connects. This offers a precise operational language for scientists and engineers.
items.title: The Thinness Index: A Transport-Based Diagnostic for Chaos in Engineered and Natural Systems

items.summary: Predictive maintenance has become one of the most important approaches for improving reliability, efficiency, and operational continuity in modern industrial enterprises. Unlike corrective maintenance, which is performed after equipment failure, and preventive maintenance, which follows predetermined schedules, predictive maintenance relies on real-time condition monitoring and data analysis to estimate the probability of future faults. The aim of this study was to analyze modern predictive maintenance methods used for industrial machinery and equipment and to evaluate their advantages, limitations, and practical applications. A literature-based analytical approach was used to examine vibration analysis, temperature monitoring, acoustic emission, oil analysis, electrical signature analysis, Internet of Things technologies, machine learning, digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based diagnostic systems. The analysis indicates that combining sensor-based monitoring with intelligent data analytics can identify abnormal equipment behavior before catastrophic failure occurs. Predictive maintenance can reduce unplanned downtime, optimize spare-parts management, extend equipment life, and decrease maintenance costs. However, successful implementation depends on sensor reliability, data quality, appropriate algorithms, integration with industrial control systems, and qualified personnel. Predictive maintenance should therefore be considered a key component of smart manufacturing and modern industrial asset management.
tags: predictive maintenance, industrial machinery, condition monitoring, machine learning, vibration analysis, IoT, digital twin, equipment reliability.
items.title: INTELLIGENT PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE TECHNOLOGIES FOR MODERN INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT

items.summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five completions (the floor axiom, bias as signal, the developmental axis, self-propagation, and the translation function) and seven operators (grounding defaults, reframes, win-win-win incentives, developmental pricing, regulation rituals, lateral social proof, and the door) specify the discipline as buildable rather than rhetorical. The research program states the core hypothesis in falsifiable form: bias magnitudes measured in the classical paradigms are partly substrate-dependent and will shift under floor restoration, tested against an active control using canonical instruments. The measurement problem is stated rather than finessed — there is no clean control group, because there is no reservoir of reliably grounded subjects and therefore no true zero — with within-subject designs, natural experiments, and dose-response gradients offered as partial routes. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. Companion to the five-essay Spine. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.

items.summary: Computational supplement for the preprint: "Relative Ternary Defect Dynamics in the Accelerated Collatz Inverse Relation" This release contains the code and reproducibility material used to audit finite instances of the main constructions in the manuscript, including: inverse-family identities; exact relative-defect recurrence; local lift-defect isometry; finite triangular bijection; countdown and recharge identities; layered-state and finite-horizon closure; precision lower-bound examples; finite-state obstruction examples; randomized and exhaustive counterexample searches. The computations are intended for reproducibility and falsification support. They do not replace the mathematical proofs and do not constitute a proof of the Collatz conjecture. items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.summary: Abstract Background Dapsone is a key component of multidrug therapy (MDT) for Hansen's disease but is associated with serious adverse effects, including methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and hepatotoxicity. The simultaneous occurrence of these complications is rare and potentially life-threatening. Early recognition is critical, especially in resource-limited settings where advanced diagnostic tools may not be readily available. Case Report The patient presented with jaundice, fever, and breathlessness approximately one month after initiation of dapsone therapy. Examination revealed pallor, icterus, and edema. Laboratory findings showed severe hyperbilirubinemia (>25 mg/dL), elevated transaminases, anemia (hemoglobin ~8 g/dL), markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase (1705 U/L), and negative Coombs test, consistent with non-immune hemolysis. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and arterial blood gas analysis indicated metabolic acidosis. Methemoglobinemia was clinically diagnosed by the treating team. Imaging revealed pleural effusion and ascites, suggesting systemic involvement. Dermatology consultation suggested dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome, and dapsone was discontinued. The overall findings were consistent with dapsone-induced multisystem toxicity involving hepatic, hematological, and respiratory systems. Conclusion This case highlights a rare but severe presentation of dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and acute liver failure. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for dapsone toxicity in patients presenting with jaundice, anemia, and respiratory symptoms shortly after initiation of therapy. Early drug withdrawal and prompt supportive management are essential to prevent life-threatening complications.
items.title: Dapsone-Induced Hemolytic Anemia, Severe Acute Liver Injury and Clinically Suspected Methemoglobinemia in a Patient with Hansen's Disease: A Rare Case Report.

items.summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.32. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial knot type is at least 6.32. The proof combines an acyclic essential-secant bootstrap, exact compatible affine radial transfers, covered joint-radius propagation, exact profile convolution, ordered failure boundaries, and retained distortion constraints through a common interior knot point. The complete computer-assisted certificate chain was run independently at 96-bit and 192-bit precision; each run certified 2,024,886 boxes across 52 sequential stages and 132 uniform regional results, with all 26 verification-source hashes frozen. This record contains the 19-page version 1.0 preprint and its complete reproducible source and verification package. The preprint has not been submitted to or accepted by a journal.
items.title: An improved lower bound for the distortion of a knotted curve

items.summary: Introduction: Carpal tunnel release is highly effective; however, a subset of patients develops persistent or recurrent symptoms requiring revision surgery. Failure may reflect incomplete decompression, perineural scarring, technical injury, or patient-related systemic and occupational factors. This study aimed to assess the incidence of revision surgery and identify its independent predictors following primary carpal tunnel release. Material and methods: This retrospective, descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Imam Reza Hospital, Tabriz, Iran, and included 300 adults who underwent primary carpal tunnel release. Eligible records were selected through convenience sampling. Demographic, clinical, electrophysiological, surgical, postoperative, and revision-related data were extracted from medical records using a standardized form and analyzed statistically to determine the incidence and predictors of revision surgery. Results: Revision carpal tunnel surgery occurred in 8.0% of patients. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative severe electrodiagnostic grade (adjusted OR=3.86, 95% CI:1.31-11.38; P=0.014), persistent postoperative pillar or scar pain (adjusted OR=3.41, 95% CI:1.18-9.85; P=0.023), primary endoscopic release (adjusted OR=3.25, 95% CI:1.04-10.15; P=0.043), preoperative thenar atrophy (adjusted OR=3.12, 95% CI:1.08-8.99; P=0.035), and diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR=2.94, 95% CI:1.05-8.24; P=0.040) as independent predictors of revision surgery. Conclusion: Secondary revision following carpal tunnel release is primarily driven by advanced baseline neural degeneration, metabolic comorbidity, endoscopic decompression, and persistent postoperative pillar pain. Comprehensive preoperative electrodiagnostic risk stratification, careful surgical technique selection, and targeted glycemic management are essential to mitigate surgical failure rates and optimize long-term clinical recovery.
items.title: Assessment of the Incidence and Predictors of Revision Surgery Following Carpal Tunnel Release

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.
items.title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 30: The Authenticity Tax

items.summary: Physical theories have been highly successful in analysing phenomena associated with motion, such as forces, trajectories, fields, and spacetime dynamics, yet comparatively little attention has been given to motion itself as a foundational problem. Across classical mechanics, quantum theory, and general relativity, motion is treated as a presupposed background condition rather than as an entity requiring ontological grounding. This paper identifies this asymmetry as a neglected issue in the foundations of physics. By examining the conceptual role of physical laws across major theoretical frameworks, it is argued that such laws constrain the form of motion without accounting for its persistent existence. This reveals a limitation common to inert ontological assumptions, according to which matter and fields lack the intrinsic capacity to sustain dynamical activity. The paper, therefore, addresses the ontic foundations of physical law alongside the problem of motion itself. To this end, the Kinetic Ground Hypothesis is introduced as a prescriptive interpretive model in which motion is understood as requiring continuous sustaining conditions rather than inertial self-maintenance. Within this framework, physical laws are reinterpreted as stable abstractions of an underlying nomological order. The grounding of motion and law is connected to consciousness through a novel model, distinct from standard fine-tuning and nomological harmony approaches, and informed by Indian philosophical metaphysics. Without altering empirical physics, the study offers an ontological clarification relevant to both foundational physics and contemporary metaphysical debate.
items.title: The Kinetic Ground Hypothesis: Addressing the Problem of Motion through Vedic Nomology

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22737224 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes It explains the problem properly, namely the need for reliable methods for miRNA analysis, as RNA-seq methods are not able to account for its specific characteristics. It also points out the gaps in prior benchmarking studies, clearly identifying that a benchmark particularly for normalization and differential expression has not been performed before, especially one incorporating recently developed methods. Lastly, it clearly states its aim and overall approach. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate 1. Some methodological details are missing. PCA and heatmap figures (figure 1B and 1C) are presented in Results alone, with no explanation in Methods section. So no information on the input data (raw or normalized or log), if it was scaled, the miRNAs selection criteria, or what clustering methods were applied. Due to this, the reproducibility of the paper is affected. 2. The paper frames as evaluating a broad range of normalization strategies but just tests only two types: within-sample scaling (RPM, RPM_total, MAP) and cross-sample (DESeq2,TMM). Other options such as quantile normalization or compositional data methods were not tested. 3. An uneven comparison in the differential expression benchmark, two different input data types used. Most methods use miRNA-level count matrix whereas miRglmm uses isomiR-level count matrix. Still, the authors do not address whether miRglmm's strong performance is due to the model or input data. 4. The underlying logic for the ground truth is circular. The authors state that DE ground truth is defined by "monotonicity trends derived from RPM values". But RPM is what they recommend for normalization. So ranking other tools against a baseline that uses their preferred method creates a feedback loop that is not validated against any independent benchmark. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported 1. The paper relies almost entirely on monotonicity as the ground-truth signal, across normalization, differential expression and log2FC tissue-specificity direction. While its limitations are acknowledged, its recommendations seem overconfident due to the narrow validation scope and too much reliance on a single criterion. 2. The authors identified pancreatic contamination in Mouse 3, clearly separating on PC2. They state that removing Mouse 3 did not alter the normalization or DE benchmarking results, but it is based only on supplementary figures and not present in the main text. So, it can not be independently verified. 3. In Results, the authors state that rlog-mean had the highest accuracy and precision for mixture proportions and the lowest error for technical replicate variability. But still the paper recommends RPM instead. The justification is that rlog-mean over-corrects the data by flattening variance between random non-replicate sample pairs.. But this relies on supplementary data and lacks quantitative statistical support in the main text. 4. No clear recommendation is made for log2FC estimation. The log2FC accuracy benchmark doesn't have a clear top method. Instead, the results show a sign-dependent split; RPM-FC and edgeR-v2 do better with positive log2FCs, and miRglmm and NBSR do better with negative log2FCs. The authors do not give a default recommendation for users. Are the data presentations, including visualizations, well-suited to represent the data? Highly appropriate and clear The visualizations are well-designed and logical for each analysis goal. These visuals communicate complex data patterns, like normalization trends and differential expression performance, in a clear format. Supplementary figure are a publication norm as well. items.summary: The Empirical-Axiomatic Framework (EAF) is a broader foundational framework concerned with existence, ontological structure, consistency, logic, information, representation, knowledge, scientific modelling, consciousness, and related philosophical questions. This paper develops the epistemological part of EAF by establishing a conceptual relation between underlying structures, representations, information, self, epistemic architecture, epistemic capacity, and knowledge. The paper distinguishes the Universal Information Space from the Ontological Information Space and defines knowledge as information possessed by a self, where a self is understood as a well-defined system. It further distinguishes generalised knowledge from Traditional Knowledge, with Traditional Knowledge requiring comprehended structural correspondence between a representation and the underlying structure it represents. The paper analyses epistemic activities, knowledge generation, representation changes, generator bases, and the limitations of epistemic systems. It distinguishes incomplete representations from incorrect representations and epistemic limitations from ontological limitations. A computer is examined as a detailed example of a non-biological epistemic system capable of acquiring, storing, processing, transforming, representing, and communicating information without these capacities necessarily implying consciousness or Traditional Knowledge. The framework is then applied to major epistemological and related philosophical problems, including induction, Gödel’s incompleteness problem, material implication, the philosophy of mathematics, Benacerraf’s problem, Gettier’s problem, demarcation, the Münchhausen trilemma, Sorites, and universals. The paper does not claim to provide final solutions to all these problems. Rather, it offers a unified conceptual basis for reframing them through the relations among existence, structure, representation, information, and epistemic systems. The resulting framework provides a foundation for further formal, scientific, and philosophical development within EAF.
items.title: Epistemology within the Empirical-Axiomatic Framework

items.summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
items.title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
items.title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

items.summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). Sample statistics Total events: 658,241 (102,699 from 1996, 555,542 from 1997–1998) Hadronic Z → qq̄: 385,583 (2000 A LR  selection) Z → e + e − : 16,547 (2001 leptonic selection) Z → μ + μ − : 13,992 (2001 leptonic selection) Z → τ + τ − : 17,133 (2001 leptonic selection) Mean particles / event: 54.4 Mean charged particles / event: 13.4 Mean |P e |: 76.14% (1996), 73.08% (1997–1998) Simulated events (Monte Carlo) New in v3.
